catalog_quote: [p.21] Vowel length[20] is phonemic and is written as VV. Heterogeneous vowel sequences occur as bimoric complex nuclei in syllable rhymes. ... Korafe has the following syllable patterns: V, CV, VV, CVV, VVV, CVVV. ... Primary stress within a word is associated with a 'heavy' syllable, a syllable which is uttered for a longer duration than the other syllables in the word. ... In a similar word biká [biᵊ.'kʰa] 'sister-in-law' receiving stress on its second syllable ... [fn.20] In Farr and Farr (1974:26), this vowel length was interpreted as word tone. ... [p.22] Stress is predictable for most of the words in Korafe. Non-verbs and verb stems manifest word stress on: (1) the initial syllable of words with two syllables (2) the second syllable of words with more than two syllables, or (3) the first (C)VV(V) syllable (when this pattern occurs). sources.citation: Farr, James B. and Cynthia J. M. Farr. 1974. A preliminary Korafe phonology. Workpapers in Papua New Guinea Languages 3: 5-38. Ukarumpa: SIL. (StressTyp2 passage 141; also Gordon 2002 NLLT 20:491-552, secondary)
sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of Korafe (34 pp) and the source StressTyp2 cites for its 'initial stress' coding that our record contradicts; reading pp. 26 ff. would document exactly what the 1974 analysis said (word tone + stress) and close the StressTyp2 contradiction note with a page citation. It would not change the coding: Farr 1996 fn.20 explicitly supersedes it.
